{{nihongo|'''Kabatakamo Shrine'''|加畑賀茂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

It is identified as one of the two seats of '''Kamo Shrine''' (かもじんじゃ), a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|Q134917287|qid=Q134917287}}. Its sacred tree is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=juniper}} said to be 1,200 years old, located across {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=National Route 136}}.

=== History ===
It is said to have been founded in the {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} era (806-810). In the ''{{ill|Izu no Kuni Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}'' it is recorded as "Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Kamo no Myōjin."

There is a tradition that Mishima Daimyōjin of {{ill|Iyo Province|Q907829|qid=Q907829}} ({{ill|Ōyamazumi Shrine|Q703904|qid=Q703904}}) landed from the {{ill|Izu Islands|Q864302|qid=Q864302}} to the {{ill|Izu Peninsula|Q822822|qid=Q822822}} at this site<ref>Shikinaisha Survey Report, Vol. 10 (Tōkaidō 5)</ref>.

Until the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the enshrined deity was {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto}}<ref>''Zushū Shikō''</ref><ref>''Jinja Kakuroku Ge''</ref>, but in the Meiji period it was changed to {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi}} in line with the deity change at {{ill|Mishima Taisha|Q650772|qid=Q650772}}.
